idea: Make codex's marketplace-index parsing more robust to a single bad plugin entry (the 2026-06-05 policy.authentication:'OFF' incident that aborted the whole index parse) WITHOUT a high upstream-canonical conflict surface, per the codex fork's overlay-first core tenet.

candidateDirections.name: Toolkit-side pre-release / CI / pre-commit schema guard
candidateDirections.summary: Validate every authentication+installation value across all three marketplace indexes against codex's accepted enum set before publish; ZERO codex conflict surface; fixes the actual root cause (our own bad data).
candidateDirections.rebaseCostNote: No codex patch, no SANDBOX-PATCH ceremony; all cost stays in toolkit-owned validation.

candidateDirections.name: Upstream-first codex partial-parse (skip-and-warn bad entries)
candidateDirections.summary: Two-stage rewrite of load_raw_marketplace_manifest: parse plugins as Vec<JsonValue> then from_value per-entry with warn-and-skip, so valid plugins survive; extends an existing skip-and-warn precedent. Pursue UPSTREAM (zero fork cost) rather than as a fork patch (INLINE).
candidateDirections.rebaseCostNote: Upstream-only avoids fork rebase cost; fork-local carry is a perpetual SANDBOX PATCH site on a function upstream may refactor.

candidateDirections.name: TUI add-error detail surfacing (diagnosis-only)
candidateDirections.summary: Thread the already-available serde error into marketplace_add_error_popup_params, mirroring the sibling marketplace_load_error_popup_params which already renders err.to_string(). Fixes the masking bug but not robustness; better upstreamed.
candidateDirections.rebaseCostNote: Small upstream-canonical TUI edit in a high-churn area; perpetual rebase friction for a UX-only win unless upstreamed.

candidateDirections.name: Tolerant enum via #[serde(other)] -> safe default (NOT recommended)
candidateDirections.summary: Mechanically feasible catch-all variant on the two policy enums, but silently accepts a malformed security-relevant authentication value instead of failing safe; strictly weaker than D-002.
candidateDirections.rebaseCostNote: Small diff but high semantic ownership cost; edits 2 upstream enums + their exhaustive From impls, forever.

questionsForSynthesis: Scope: protect only our marketplace, or arbitrary third-party marketplaces a codex user adds? (If only ours, D-001 alone suffices.)
Should unknown authentication values always fail closed (drop the plugin) rather than be silently defaulted? (Favors D-002 over D-004.)
Must a skipped/dropped plugin be VISIBLE in the TUI, not just warn! to tracing? (Couples D-002 with D-003.)
Are we willing to upstream the codex-side change instead of carrying it as a fork patch?
holdReason: Autonomous brainstorm; HOLD for operator review before any plan/impl. 3-lens + Devil's-Advocate consensus (red_flag=true) that fork-local codex hardening is net-negative vs the toolkit guard; codex robustness work is worth doing only as an upstream contribution.
